title: Nobody noticed your stumble
text: The effect was demonstrated in a famous experiment {{1}} students wore an embarrassing T-shirt into a room {{2}} observers, then estimated how many had noticed. The students' guesses were roughly double the true figure, {{3}} surprised nobody who has ever left the house with bed-hair. {{4}} is the spotlight effect: we dramatically overestimate how closely other people watch us, because we each mistake our own inner spotlight for the general lighting. {{5}} a result, small embarrassments loom far larger than they are. Remembering the effect is oddly comforting: the audience we fear is {{6}} busy rehearsing its own entrance to grade ours. Most of the time, {{7}} one is watching at all, {{8}} turns out to be the most liberating discovery an anxious mind can make.

gaps.explanation: 'Where' refers back to the room as the place.
'A room of observers' — the room's contents take 'of'.
Sentential relative after the comma summarising the overestimate.
'This is…' — the near demonstrative introducing the named effect.
'As a result' is the fixed linking phrase.

gaps.hint: adverb: is ___ busy rehearsing to grade ours
gaps.explanation: 'Too busy … to' — the excess that prevents the grading.

gaps.hint: determiner: ___ one is watching at all
relative: ___, __ turns out to be liberating
gaps.explanation: Sentential relative after the comma; 'that' is impossible here.
